To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a combination of inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)/long-acting beta2-adrenoceptor agonist (LABA) is associated with increased risk of asthma-related hospitalizations, and that the use of an ICS alone is not associated with this risk.

fluticasone furoate/vilanterol 100/25 micrograms twice daily is effective in reducing asthma exacerbations in patients with moderate-to-severe asthma and that fluticason propionate 500 micrograms twice daily, fluticasone 500 micrograms plus formoterol 10 micrograms twice daily or salmeterol 50 micrograms twice daily had similar efficacy in reducing asthma exacerbation rates.
the addition of fluticasone to salmeterol is associated with a significant improvement in lung function in patients with asthma who are inadequately controlled on salmeterol monotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of salmeterol in the treatment of asthma in children.
the use of fluticasone nasal spray in the prevention of asthma attacks and in the treatment of nasal symptoms in patients with allergic rhinitis.
the use of fluticasone in the treatment of asthma and COPD, and we have demonstrated that fluticasone is an effective and safe treatment in both diseases, with a good tolerability profile.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of fluticasone/salmeterol is a very good option for the treatment of patients with COPD, and that it should be considered as a first-line treatment option in patients with severe COPD.
salmeterol is not indicated as a first line treatment of asthma.

the use of salmeterol and fluticasone in combination is more effective than the use of fluticasone alone in reducing the frequency of exacerbations and improving lung function in patients with asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the Diskus inhaler is associated with a significant reduction in exacerbations, compared with the MDI, and that this reduction is not associated with any increase in side effects.
the addition of fluticasone to salmeterol provides a significant improvement in asthma control over either drug alone.
fluticasone and salmeterol combination inhalation powder is a safe and effective treatment for asthma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

fluticasone furoate and fluticasone/salmeterol have comparable effects on the lung and systemic corticosteroid exposure in patients with COPD, and fluticasome/salmeterol is more effective than fluticasone in improving dyspnoea and lung function in these patients.
the use of salmeterol and fluticasone in the treatment of asthma is not associated with increased cardiovascular risk.
the combination of fluticasone and salmeterol is not a good treatment option for children with mild to moderate asthma.
